title: English 11–12: rhetoric, research and professional writing
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Read American, British and world literature in context, analyze and synthesize arguments, read science writing and data, master research and citation, and write college essays and professional messages.

blocks.deliverable: Connect a text to its historical context.
Write a rhetorical analysis and a short synthesis.
Build an argument that answers its strongest objection.
Week 7 midterm; summarize a science news article and check its claims against the study.
Build an annotated bibliography in APA style.
Draft a personal essay and a professional email.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Researched argument of about 1,500 words on a health-policy question, using five cited sources and presenting the main positions fairly, plus a personal-essay draft.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
